items.title: My FPL GW9 Free Hit Team! 💥 #fpl
items.headline: Haaland is the standout Free Hit captain for Gameweek 9 as Spurs defence anchors the draft
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear captaincy pick in a provisional Free Hit squad for Gameweek 9, with Manchester City hosting Brighton. The forward offers the safest combination of ceiling and reliability in the one-week team, while the draft also includes Thiago as a short-term punt against Nottingham Forest. Thiago has produced an attacking return in four straight matches, takes penalties and is expected to play 90 minutes; he is not viewed as strong long-term value, but his home fixture makes him attractive for a Free Hit. Nicolas Jackson is the other forward named, with Fulham the opposition.

Caoimhin Kelleher starts in goal for the home match against Nottingham Forest, identified as the league's weakest attack. Forest's poor finishing is seen as helpful not only for clean-sheet potential but also for save points. The defence doubles on Tottenham, with Pedro Porro and Jan Paul van Hecke selected for Crystal Palace at home. Spurs have the best clean-sheet odds of the gameweek, and while their attack has disappointed as an FPL source, their underlying defensive numbers remain encouraging. Porro adds set-piece involvement and attacking upside, while Van Hecke and Antonio Silva are picked partly for defensive-contribution potential; Silva faces Leeds at home.

Chelsea's home game against Manchester United drives a midfield double-up on Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, with United considered vulnerable under their unchanged manager. Manzambi is included for Fulham because of his strong attacking volume, while Tavernier earns a place on current form. The draft is built around favourable home fixtures, clean-sheet probability and one-week upside rather than long-term price value.

The Free Hit is not confirmed, however. Its use depends on late injury news in the existing squad, so the proposed XI is a strong Gameweek 9 template rather than a locked-in final team.
key_points: Captain Haaland at home to Brighton in Gameweek 9.
Start Kelleher against Nottingham Forest, whose weak attack could provide both clean-sheet and save-point potential.
Double up on Spurs defenders Porro and Van Hecke for Crystal Palace at home, the gameweek's leading clean-sheet fixture.
Porro is preferred for his set pieces and attacking threat, while Van Hecke and Antonio Silva offer defensive-contribution routes to points.
Back Palmer and Rogers against Manchester United, with Chelsea expected to exploit United's defensive weakness.
Thiago is a one-week Free Hit punt against Nottingham Forest after four consecutive attacking returns, with penalties and likely 90 minutes strengthening the case.
Delay activating the Free Hit until injury news clarifies whether the existing squad requires the chip.

items.headline: Haaland is the clear Gameweek 9 captain as Jackson replaces injured João Pedro
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the straightforward captain for Gameweek 9, with Manchester City hosting Southampton. The goalkeeper situation is less appealing, with David Raya facing Liverpool, but a goalkeeper transfer is not considered worthwhile this week.

The defence is built around Jan Paul van Hecke, who has both a favourable Wolves fixture and some attacking upside, plus Lewis Hall at home to Everton. Hall is not a priority buy and could be sold in the near future, but he is a good enough starter for this round. Gabriel forms an Arsenal defensive double-up with Riccardo Calafiori, although Calafiori is benched while yellow-flagged. If Calafiori is ruled out beyond the international break, he is likely to be sold for Manchester City’s Bernardo Silva, with Ezri Konsa dropping to the bench; if he has a chance of returning for Gameweek 10, he is worth holding.

Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers stay despite Chelsea’s poor display against Liverpool and João Pedro’s injury. Their upcoming schedules remain favourable enough to justify patience. Evanilson also keeps his place after blanking on his debut in the squad: with Enes Ünal ruled out until January, the Bournemouth forward should receive regular minutes as the central striker. Bryan Mbeumo has a difficult trip to Manchester City in Gameweek 9, but Brentford’s fixtures improve markedly from Gameweek 10, so he is retained.

The early transfer is João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson, completed before the price changes. João Pedro is expected to miss at least the period before the international break, while Jackson offers a more secure short-term route into Chelsea’s attack and benefits from their good fixtures.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland against Southampton in Gameweek 9.
Transfer João Pedro out for Nicolas Jackson after João Pedro’s injury is expected to keep him out until at least the international break.
Start Jan Paul van Hecke for Brighton’s home match against Wolves, with his set-piece and goal threat adding appeal.
Lewis Hall starts against Everton but remains a potential future sale rather than a player to buy now.
Hold Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers because their fixture runs remain strong despite recent underwhelming returns.
Keep Evanilson as Bournemouth’s likely first-choice No. 9 while Enes Ünal is out until January.
Monitor Riccardo Calafiori’s fitness: sell him for Bernardo Silva if his absence extends beyond the international break, but hold if he can return for Gameweek 10.
Retain Bryan Mbeumo through Manchester City away because Brentford’s fixtures improve from Gameweek 10.

items.headline: Palmer makes way as Haaland, Isak and Gabriel anchor a Gameweek 9 Wildcard
items.summary:
A Gameweek 9 Wildcard is under serious consideration after a difficult round featuring injuries and Cole Palmer’s red card. The existing squad has too many concerns: Riccardo Calafiori carries a flag and may face reduced minutes during a congested spell, Palmer has underperformed for much of the season, Morgan Gibbs-White has lacked end product, João Pedro is injured, and Thomas may be absent for an extended period. The proposed reset also moves away from Mbeumo despite his returns, with Manchester United still not trusted as an attacking proposition.

The defensive core is built around a Kinsky-Trafford goalkeeper rotation, which is viewed as particularly favourable because of the upcoming home fixtures. Leif Davis, Mohamovic and Gabriel form the main defence, with Gabriel preferred to Calafiori despite the higher price because of his security and attacking potential. Mohamovic is also backed as a regular starter alongside Uskovic, except in prohibitive fixtures such as Arsenal or Manchester City.

The midfield sacrifices Palmer for Morgan Rogers, Antoine Semenyo, Marcus Tavernier and Rodon, with Tavernier selected after a strong start to the campaign. Groves is temporarily benched for the Manchester City away fixture but is expected to return to the side in Gameweek 10. Up front, the Wildcard keeps premium firepower through Erling Haaland and Alexander Isak, while Nicolas Jackson supplies form and depth; Consor is retained as a bench option.

The appeal of the structure is that it avoids an expensive midfield premium and creates a strong 15-man squad, with multiple playable options and likely price rises. The downside is persistent benching dilemmas and inevitable bench points, particularly with Bench Boost no longer available. There is concern about selling Palmer before Manchester United because of his penalty potential, but Chelsea’s poor form and João Pedro’s injury reduce confidence that Palmer’s output will improve immediately.
key_points: A Gameweek 9 Wildcard is favoured after injuries, Palmer’s red card and several underperforming players leave the current squad needing a reset.
Gabriel is preferred to flagged Calafiori because Calafiori’s minutes may be less secure during the Champions League and Christmas schedule.
Kinsky and Trafford are selected as a rotating goalkeeper pair on the strength of their upcoming home-fixture rotation.
Palmer is sold for Morgan Rogers, with Chelsea’s poor form and João Pedro’s injury judged to outweigh Palmer’s penalty appeal against Manchester United.
Haaland, Isak and Jackson form the attacking core, giving the squad two elite captaincy options plus Jackson’s current form.
Tavernier is a midfield differential after his strong start, while Groves is only benched for the Manchester City away match before returning in Gameweek 10.
The no-premium-midfield structure creates a deep squad but brings weekly selection problems and the risk of significant bench points.

items.title: FPL GW9 EXPERT Transfer Trends & Best Captain! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 9 Team Plans
items.headline: João Pedro exit fuels Nicolas Jackson rush as Haaland dominates Gameweek 9 captaincy
items.summary:
Gameweek 9 is a clear action week for Fantasy Premier League managers, with 47% of surveyed experts making one transfer, 28% making two and 17% making three or more. Only 2% roll a transfer, while around 7% deploy a Wildcard or Free Hit. The high activity reflects a combination of injuries, squad clean-up and attractive fixture runs, particularly for Aston Villa and Bournemouth assets.

João Pedro is the standout sell after news that he is expected to miss at least two gameweeks. Eighty per cent of the experts who own him move him on, making João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson the overwhelmingly preferred transfer. Jackson is viewed as a long-term pick rather than a one-week punt: Aston Villa have an extended favourable run, he is rested in midweek and begins with Fulham at home in Gameweek 9. Gonzalo to Jackson and Wissa to Jackson are also strongly backed routes into the Villa forward.

If a second striker transfer is needed, experts are more willing to consider Alexander Isak or Evanilson, although Jackson is markedly preferred as the primary replacement. Isak offers upside but is a less comfortable immediate buy because of Arsenal, while Evanilson is generally treated as a secondary forward move rather than the direct João Pedro successor. In midfield, Tavernier is a leading buy ahead of Leeds at home, with Saka, Sangaré and Cherki among the suggested sales. Manzambi is the cheaper alternative for managers unable to afford Tavernier.

Defensively, Silva is the most popular incoming defender, with Gabriel, Van Hecke and Hill also attracting interest. Calafiori is a more nuanced decision: some managers sell because his availability for Gameweek 10 is uncertain and they want Arsenal defensive cover then, but most hold for now in case he is fit for Gameweek 9 or clearer news emerges. Cherki, King, Wissa and Gonzalo are among other commonly sold players, while experts generally resist the wider-market urge to sell Cole Palmer; every expert owner keeps him.

Captaincy is close to unanimous. Erling Haaland, owned by 99% of the expert group, receives 93% of captain votes for Brighton at home. Palmer away to Manchester United is the only meaningful alternative at 5%, helped by the fact that he has already served his suspension in the League Cup and is available for the Premier League fixture. Nicolas Jackson and Thiago receive isolated differential captaincy support, but Haaland remains the safe and overwhelmingly recommended choice.
key_points: Sell João Pedro if possible: he is expected to miss at least Gameweeks 9 and 10, and 80% of expert owners transfer him out.
Nicolas Jackson is the priority forward buy, especially for João Pedro, Gonzalo or Wissa owners, due to Aston Villa's long favourable fixture run and Fulham at home in Gameweek 9.
Use Isak or Evanilson mainly as second-forward replacements rather than ahead of Jackson; Isak's Arsenal fixture reduces his immediate appeal.
Tavernier is the leading midfield transfer for Leeds at home, with Saka, Sangaré and Cherki viable routes out.
Silva is the preferred defensive buy, while Calafiori owners largely wait for further fitness news rather than selling immediately.
Captain Haaland against Brighton at home; Palmer is the main differential alternative against Manchester United.
Gameweek 9 is not viewed as a week to roll: 92% of experts make at least one transfer or use a chip, with about 7% on a Wildcard or Free Hit.

items.headline: Haaland captains a budget-heavy Gameweek 9 Wildcard as premium midfielders are ignored
items.summary:
A Gameweek 9 Wildcard is built around Erling Haaland as the only essential premium, with the Manchester City striker handed the captaincy almost every week because no high-priced midfielder is producing consistently enough to justify the investment. Nicolas Jackson takes the vice-captaincy, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin completes the forward line; Evan Ferguson is presented as a viable alternative in that third-striker slot.

David Raya remains the preferred goalkeeper despite Arsenal travelling to Liverpool in Gameweek 9. The defence prioritises low-cost starters, with Antonio Silva, Chris Mepham and Jan Paul van Hecke included to free funds for an Arsenal double-up featuring Gabriel. Ezri Konsa is a more uncertain pick because of the possible return of William Saliba, while Calafiori is flagged, and Jarrad Branthwaite is also part of the defensive options.

The midfield deliberately avoids Bruno Fernandes, Bukayo Saka and Cole Palmer. Morgan Rogers is the most expensive midfielder selected, valued as a well-priced route into Chelsea's attack when the side clicks. Pascal Gross keeps his place despite facing Manchester City in Gameweek 9 after coming close to an attacking return against Liverpool in Gameweek 8, while Marcus Tavernier and Manzambi provide cheaper midfield cover.

Cody Gakpo is retained as a bench option even though he faces Gabriel this week, with Liverpool's fixtures improving significantly from Gameweek 10 onwards. The central Wildcard trade-off is accepting budget and rotation risks in defence and midfield in exchange for Haaland, Jackson and a stronger forward-heavy structure, rather than spreading funds across several premium midfielders.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 9 and is expected to keep the armband most weeks in this Wildcard structure.
Nicolas Jackson is vice-captain, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin selected up front and Evan Ferguson offered as an alternative.
David Raya is retained despite Arsenal's away fixture against Liverpool in Gameweek 9.
Gabriel provides an Arsenal defensive double-up, while Antonio Silva, Chris Mepham and Jan Paul van Hecke are budget defensive enablers.
The midfield excludes Bruno Fernandes, Bukayo Saka and Cole Palmer, with Morgan Rogers the most expensive midfielder selected.
Pascal Gross remains despite Manchester City in Gameweek 9 after nearly returning against Liverpool in Gameweek 8.
Cody Gakpo is held for Liverpool's stronger fixture run from Gameweek 10, even though he faces Arsenal this week.
Konsa carries uncertainty around Saliba's return, while Calafiori is yellow-flagged.

items.title: My FPL GW9 TEAM SELECTION! 🔥 KEEP JOAO PEDRO? 👀
items.headline: Haaland remains captain as Thiaw exit takes priority over João Pedro injury
items.summary:
A 45-point Gameweek 8 produces a small red arrow amid a volatile round in which many popular midfielders — Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White and Bryan Mbeumo — blank, while Palmer is sent off against Spurs. The major regret is retaining Newcastle defender Malick Thiaw, who is benched alongside Sven Botman as Dan Burn and Fabian Schär keep a clean sheet. Thiaw is now a clear sell after losing his place and delivering a damaging swing against Lewis Hall since the Gameweek 3 wildcard.

The Gameweek 9 plan is to sell Thiaw for Bournemouth’s Silva rather than immediately move out injured Chelsea forward João Pedro. Silva combines strong defensive-contribution numbers, Bournemouth’s third-best expected-goals-conceded record, and a favourable long-term fixture run; Arsenal away is the only clearly difficult match in the next eight. Jan Paul van Hecke remains a reliable hold because Brighton’s schedule allows him to start in almost every upcoming week, while Mendy is worth starting against Ipswich if he returns to training as expected.

João Pedro’s thigh injury is expected to rule him out until at least Gameweek 11, but the case for selling depends on squad context. With one free transfer, replacing Thiaw allows a playable 4-4-2 over the next two weeks rather than forcing a sale of Pedro for a forward who may not be the preferred long-term choice. A hit is avoided because Jackson, despite his recent brace, could block future moves for Dominic Calvert-Lewin or funds needed to buy Gabriel. Calvert-Lewin is particularly appealing as a prospective Gameweek 12 captain, when Erling Haaland faces Arsenal and the main midfield alternatives have awkward fixtures.

Haaland is the straightforward Gameweek 9 captain after receiving a full League Cup rest, with Palmer vice-captain despite his suspension also giving him a midweek break. Manchester City lead the projected-goals rankings at 2.3, ahead of Spurs on 2.2 and Chelsea on 2.0. Palmer and Mbeumo have upside in Chelsea v Manchester United, given United’s poor form and Chelsea’s defensive absences, while Sharda remains a riskier starter after an early substitution but retains a high ceiling at home to Forest.

Looking further ahead, Blank Gameweek 30 may not require a Free Hit. Brighton v Coventry, Forest v Villa and Hull v Chelsea are confirmed to go ahead, and Sunderland’s cup exit would also keep Arsenal’s match alive. Managers with Raya or another active goalkeeper could therefore navigate the round without a chip, preserving flexibility for later doubles or blanks.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 9, with Cole Palmer as vice-captain after both avoid League Cup minutes.
Sell Malick Thiaw for Bournemouth’s Silva, whose defensive numbers and fixtures make him a strong long-term replacement.
Hold João Pedro for now despite his thigh injury, provided the bench can cover him and there are no more urgent squad problems.
Avoid a minus-four for João Pedro to Jackson unless it is clearly needed, as Dominic Calvert-Lewin may be the more useful future target and frees funds for Gabriel.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is under consideration for Gameweek 10 or 11 and could be a leading captaincy option in Gameweek 12.
Start Mendy against Ipswich if he is confirmed fit, while Jan Paul van Hecke is a long-term hold through Brighton’s favourable run.
Blank Gameweek 30 may be manageable without a Free Hit after several fixtures are confirmed, with Arsenal also likely to play if Sunderland exit the cup.

items.title: MY FPL GW9 TEAM SELECTION! 📱 1 FT & 3 INJURED PLAYERS... 😭  | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Hold Joao Pedro if possible as Jackson tops the Gameweek 9 forward shortlist
items.summary:
Gameweek 8 brings a red arrow from just outside the top 700,000 to around one million after returns from David Raya, Micky van de Ven and captain Erling Haaland do little to offset Cole Palmer’s red card and a string of blanks. The Gameweek 9 squad has only one free transfer and three major fitness concerns: Joao Pedro, Riccardo Calafiori and Bobby Thomas. Joao Pedro is expected to miss Manchester United and Sunderland, making Gameweek 11 against Leeds his likeliest return point, although a longer absence remains possible. Calafiori appears the most likely of the three to be available for Arsenal’s trip to Liverpool, while Thomas’s status is unclear and an absence against Sunderland looks more probable.

The preferred move is to sell Gonzalo Garcia rather than the injured Joao Pedro and bring in Jackson. Garcia has blanked in every match since his six-point Gameweek 1 and is unlikely to be a useful starter even if retained, whereas holding Joao Pedro could avoid spending another transfer to buy him back if he returns after the international break. Jackson is the leading replacement despite Aston Villa’s imperfect overall attacking numbers: their recent data has improved, he has a favourable seven-to-eight-gameweek fixture run and looks playable every week. The drawbacks are a lack of penalties, occasional early substitutions and European rotation.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is considered the safer long-term, cheaper forward but has a heavily home-weighted appeal, with difficult away trips including Bournemouth, Chelsea and Manchester City. Evanilson is attractive because Bournemouth’s upcoming fixtures are strong, though Junior’s return could affect his minutes or role. Barry and Costulas offer budget routes that could fund upgrades elsewhere, but their fixtures and reliability make them less appealing now; Costulas also faces Manchester City in Gameweek 9.

A one-transfer plan leaves an uncomfortable Gameweek 9 XI, likely with Raya, Calafiori, van de Ven, van Hecke and De Cuyper in defence; Palmer, Rogers, Gibbs-White and Gross in midfield; and Haaland plus Jackson up front. Haaland is the clear captain, with Jackson vice-captain. If Calafiori, Thomas and Joao Pedro all appear unavailable, a minus-four becomes realistic, most likely by selling Joao Pedro alongside Garcia or Slater. The priority is not necessarily to avoid another short-term red arrow, but to preserve transfers and arrive in better shape for Gameweek 11, when Joao Pedro could return and the squad’s fixtures improve.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the Gameweek 9 captaincy lock, with Jackson currently the vice-captain.
Joao Pedro is expected to miss Gameweeks 9 and 10, but may return for Chelsea’s home match against Leeds in Gameweek 11.
Gonzalo Garcia is the preferred forward sale because his sustained blanks make him less valuable than retaining Joao Pedro through injury.
Jackson is the leading replacement thanks to Aston Villa’s improving recent attack and a strong longer-term fixture run.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the safer budget-forward alternative, while Evanilson is a viable Bournemouth fixture play with some minutes risk.
Riccardo Calafiori has the best chance of playing among the flagged trio, but Arsenal are unlikely to provide a clear pre-deadline update.
If Calafiori and Bobby Thomas are ruled out as well as Joao Pedro, a minus-four to remove two problem players is under serious consideration.
Palmer and Gibbs-White remain under review, but selling either for a hit is not viewed as the immediate priority.

items.title: 1 transfer 🔒 Time for another? 🤔 My FPL Team for GW9 🔥
items.headline: Haaland reclaiming captaincy as Jackson arrival sets up a Gameweek 12 Bruno Fernandes punt
items.summary:
Andy sits inside the top 100k despite a disappointing 42-point Gameweek 8, when captaining Cole Palmer over Erling Haaland produced a damaging red-card blank. Haaland's return reinforces the safer approach: he is captain for Manchester City's home match against Brighton in Gameweek 9, with no compelling alternative among Nicolas Jackson, Palmer or Morgan Rogers. Palmer remains a hold despite his recent issues, while Bryan Mbeumo is retained as Manchester United's primary goal threat and likely regular No. 9, even with Chelsea away next.

The early transfer is João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson, made ahead of price changes. Jackson faces Fulham at home and remains a strong Villa attacking option even if João Pedro returns after the international break, although the move is not without regret: keeping João Pedro and upgrading Mamadou Sangaré to Marcus Tavernier was a viable route. Tavernier is appealing for Bournemouth's fixtures, but would create immediate selection problems by forcing Pascal Groß to the bench against Manchester City and potentially Jackson out in Gameweek 10. Sangaré is therefore kept for now despite a price fall, with Tavernier, Ezri Konsa? No—Aston Villa's Manzambi, Ipswich's Enciso and Sunderland's Enzo Le Fée all considered possible later eighth-attacker replacements.

Defensively, patience is the preferred strategy. Jan Paul van Hecke starts against Crystal Palace and Lewis Hall is playable at home to Everton, while David Raya and Ezri Konsa face Liverpool and Yankuba Minteh's return threatens Diego Gomez's longer-term minutes. Riccardo Calafiori is only sold if he is confirmed to miss both Gameweeks 9 and 10; otherwise his upside and Arsenal's Gameweek 10 home fixture against Hull justify waiting. Bournemouth's Marcos Senesi is the likely replacement if Calafiori becomes an issue, with Leeds' Murillo and Brighton's Vuskovic also future targets. Gabriel is attractive, particularly for Hull at home, but reaching him would require two transfers and is not deemed worthwhile now.

The longer-term idea is to carry transfers through Gameweek 10 and reassess after the international break. The £1.9m banked makes a Gameweek 12 switch from Palmer to Bruno Fernandes conceivable if Manchester United improve and Fernandes returns consistently to a central attacking role. Fernandes would be a major differential for Brentford at home in Gameweek 12, while Haaland has Arsenal away and may be worth opposing for captaincy. It is only a contingency, not an immediate plan: the current expectation is no further Gameweek 9 move unless Calafiori's injury news worsens, followed by a likely three free transfers in Gameweek 10 and four after the break.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the Gameweek 9 captain at home to Brighton after the Palmer captaincy gamble failed in Gameweek 8.
João Pedro is sold early for Nicolas Jackson, who starts against Fulham at home; the move is viewed as good but not unquestionably better than a Sangaré-to-Tavernier upgrade.
Riccardo Calafiori is held unless he is ruled out for both Gameweeks 9 and 10; Marcos Senesi is the preferred cheaper defensive replacement.
Lewis Hall starts against Everton at home, while Van Hecke is also favoured against Crystal Palace; Raya and Konsa must face Liverpool.
Mamadou Sangaré is retained despite falling to £5.4m, with Tavernier, Manzambi, Enciso and Enzo Le Fée among later options for the eighth-attacker slot.
Palmer and Mbeumo are held for flexibility, with Mbeumo backed by his central role and United's relatively acceptable medium-term fixtures.
A Palmer-to-Bruno Fernandes move is being considered for Gameweek 12, when United host Brentford and Haaland visits Arsenal, but only if United's performances improve.
The plan is to avoid an unnecessary second Gameweek 9 transfer, roll into Gameweek 10 and ideally reach the international break with four free transfers.

items.title: FPL GW9 Transfer Tips! | Buy, Sell, Keep, Avoid #fpl
items.headline: Johan Manzambi is the Gameweek 9 buy as Aston Villa’s fixture run begins
items.summary:
Johan Manzambi is the leading Gameweek 9 transfer target, edging out Jackson as the preferred route into Aston Villa’s attack. Villa enter an excellent eight-game fixture run, and Manzambi’s underlying numbers make him especially compelling: he averages 3.8 shots and 1.8 key passes per match despite still building fitness and playing reduced minutes. While other midfielders may post stronger high-quality-chance numbers, Manzambi stands out for sheer attacking involvement and volume.

Gonzalo Garcia is the primary sell, with Joshua King also a viable departure for managers holding him. Fulham assets initially looked attractive compared with players from the newly promoted sides because of their fixtures, but the attack is not creating enough and has been unconvincing with the chances it does produce. With Fulham’s schedule worsening from Gameweek 9 onwards, their limited attacking output offers little reason to persist.

Cole Palmer is a clear keep. Some managers may wrongly believe he is suspended in Gameweek 9, but his ban applies only to Chelsea’s League Cup tie against Liverpool. Palmer is available for the league meeting with a struggling Manchester United side, retaining his usual 90-minute security, penalties, set pieces and explosive ceiling. Selling him before that fixture carries major regret potential.

Maxim De Cuyper is the player to avoid. Brighton travel to Manchester City in Gameweek 9, a fixture that offers little clean-sheet potential and limited scope for De Cuyper’s attacking threat. His biggest scores generally require both an attacking return and a clean sheet, so existing owners should bench him where possible, while non-owners are advised to wait at least another week before considering a move.
key_points: Buy Johan Manzambi for Gameweek 9 as Aston Villa begin a favourable eight-game fixture run.
Manzambi averages 3.8 shots and 1.8 key passes per game despite limited minutes while building fitness.
Sell Gonzalo Garcia, with Joshua King also expendable, as Fulham’s attacking output is weak and their fixtures deteriorate.
Keep Cole Palmer: he is suspended only for Chelsea’s League Cup match against Liverpool, not the Gameweek 9 league fixture against Manchester United.
Palmer remains a high-upside option because he is expected to play 90 minutes and retains penalties and set-piece responsibility.
Avoid buying Brighton defender Maxim De Cuyper before the away trip to Manchester City; current owners should bench him if possible.

items.title: FPL WATCHLIST GW9 WITH FPL HARRY 🔎 | GABRIEL, TAVERNIER & JACKSON | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Nicolas Jackson leads the João Pedro replacement hunt as FPL managers reassess premium defenders
items.summary:
Gameweek 8 leaves managers with widespread problems: João Pedro is absent, Cole Palmer is sent off, Bukayo Saka is injured and several cheap defenders face fitness or selection doubts. Erling Haaland remains the clear captain for Gameweek 9 despite a modest recent return, while Palmer is retained for now because his suspension does not apply immediately and selling him before a favourable fixture is viewed as premature. Morgan Gibbs-White, Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are underwhelming but are generally lower-priority sales than injured players or non-playing forwards.

João Pedro's absence pushes Nicolas Jackson to the front of the forward market. Jackson has strong upcoming fixtures, including Coventry, Crystal Palace, Ipswich, Fulham and Sunderland, and Unai Emery appears to trust him ahead of Tammy Abraham. However, he is not a flawless pick: his underlying numbers are ordinary, he is not on penalties, he may not play 90 minutes every week and Champions League commitments create some risk. Evanilson, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Alexander Isak are viable alternatives, with Calvert-Lewin particularly appealing as a home-fixture rotation forward and penalty taker. Isak has an excellent longer-term Liverpool schedule after Arsenal, but his price, fitness record, likely Christmas rotation and the possible return of Dominik Szoboszlai on penalties temper the appeal. Managers who can cope without João Pedro briefly are encouraged to consider keeping him rather than spending transfers to sell and buy him back.

Gabriel's 17-point haul renews the case for paying £8.0m for Arsenal's most secure defender. With Saka, Palmer and Fernandes no longer demanding premium midfield investment, funds can be shifted into Arsenal's clean-sheet potential and Gabriel's set-piece threat. Riccardo Calafiori remains a cheaper route but carries recurring rotation and fitness concerns, particularly when he starts midweek; Gabriel offers the comfort of reliable festive minutes. Cristhian Mosquera is cheap and capable of returns, but William Saliba's eventual return makes his long-term starts uncertain. For immediate defensive transfers, Antonio Silva, Marcos Senesi/Mahmoudovic-type Bournemouth options and Jan Paul van Hecke are preferred budget targets, with Van Hecke and Bournemouth defenders offering clean-sheet, defensive-contribution and attacking routes to points.

Antoine Semenyo's Bournemouth team-mates also merit attention, especially Marcus Tavernier at around £6.4m. Bournemouth rank highly for both expected goals and expected goals conceded, Tavernier is playing regular minutes and is heavily involved in their attack, but his recent goals have contained fortunate elements. He is a sensible replacement for a weak or injured midfielder, yet moving Gibbs-White or Mbeumo solely for Tavernier is considered a luxury while squads have more urgent issues. Leeds midfielder Manzambi is cheaper but has less secure minutes. The recommended approach for Gameweek 9 is to avoid forcing multiple moves in an awkward fixture slate, prioritise a reliable forward replacement for Gonzalo Garcia or João Pedro where necessary, and carry transfers into Gameweek 10 when fixture swings and team news are clearer.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 9; Palmer is a credible vice-captain but Haaland remains the safer default.
Nicolas Jackson is the leading João Pedro replacement, although Evanilson, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Alexander Isak are legitimate alternatives with different price and minutes trade-offs.
Avoid selling João Pedro if the squad can cover his absence, as buying him back soon may cost another transfer and disrupt team structure.
Gabriel is increasingly attractive at £8.0m because premium midfielders are underperforming and he is more secure than Calafiori or Mosquera over the festive period.
Calafiori is likely to remain usable in the short term but midweek starts are a warning sign for Premier League rotation, especially around Europe.
Antonio Silva and Jan Paul van Hecke are favoured defensive buys for Gameweek 9, while Bobby Thomas is only worth considering if fitness news is positive.
Marcus Tavernier is a strong Bournemouth midfield option, but moving Gibbs-White or Mbeumo to him is best treated as a luxury transfer rather than an urgent fix.
A Free Hit is not favoured in Gameweek 9 because the fixture list lacks enough standout attacks to justify using the chip.

items.title: TOP 10 FPL GW9 PLAYERS TO BUY! 🎯 BEST FPL GW9 TRANSFER TIPS #fpl  #premierleague #football
items.headline: Tavernier and Jackson lead Gameweek 9 draft targets as Bournemouth and Aston Villa fixtures appeal
items.summary:
Bournemouth midfielder Marcus Tavernier is the leading Gameweek 9 midfield target after becoming central to the side’s attacking play. Despite being less attractive in previous periods, his current role and Bournemouth’s favourable long-term fixture run make him the preferred addition. Aston Villa’s Manzambi ranks next on the strength of Villa’s recent form and a promising schedule, while Everton’s Morgan Gibbs-White is the differential choice because of his set-piece duties, open-play threat and upcoming fixtures.

Up front, Aston Villa’s Jackson is the standout option after scoring twice against Manchester City in Gameweek 8. He hosts Fulham in Gameweek 9 before a trip to Manchester United, and his form makes him the top forward target despite the tougher fixture to follow. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is second: he travels to Bournemouth this week but offers strong longer-term fixtures, penalty duties, security of starts and no European rotation concerns. Evan Ferguson completes the forward shortlist, with good form and an appealing fixture run supporting his case.

Leeds defender Mepham is the preferred defensive signing even though his Gameweek 9 trip to Bournemouth is the least appealing immediate fixture among the picks. Leeds are viewed as the best-value defence in this price range, with Mepham trusted for both clean-sheet potential and attacking threat. Bournemouth’s Antonio Silva is another long-term option after clean sheets in each of the past two matches, while Spurs’ Van Hecke is backed by improved defensive displays and favourable upcoming fixtures.

For managers needing a goalkeeper, Kinski at £4.4m is the recommended buy. His price and strong long-term fixture schedule make him the preferred budget route between the posts.
key_points: Marcus Tavernier is the top midfield target for Gameweek 9 because he is focal to Bournemouth’s attack and has favourable long-term fixtures.
Aston Villa forward Jackson ranks first after his two-goal display against Manchester City in Gameweek 8, with Fulham at home next.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin offers a secure minutes pick with penalties, no European rotation and an attractive fixture run after Bournemouth away.
Mepham is the leading defender despite facing Bournemouth in Gameweek 9, owing to Leeds’ defensive value and his attacking upside.
Morgan Gibbs-White is the midfield differential, combining set pieces and open-play threat for Everton.
Kinski, priced at £4.4m, is the preferred goalkeeper option because of his long-term fixtures.

items.title: JOAO PEDRO OUT FOR "WEEKS" 🇧🇷 MY FPL GW9 TRANSFER TARGETS! ♻️  | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: João Pedro injury pushes Jackson and Tavernier to the top of Gameweek 9 transfer plans
items.summary:
João Pedro is ruled out for a few weeks with a thigh injury, making him unavailable for Manchester United and almost certainly Sunderland, with Gameweek 11 against Leeds also uncertain. He is generally a sell, although managers short of free transfers can justify holding because he could quickly become desirable again if he returns after the international break. The injury also changes squad spending: with Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes and Bukayo Saka either underperforming, injured or difficult to justify, funds can move into a premium defender such as Gabriel or a stronger forward line.

Bournemouth have the most attractive sustained fixture run and pair it with strong underlying attacking and defensive numbers. Tavernier is the standout midfield target despite some fortunate recent goals: his central role, improving output and fixtures support the move at £6.4m. Evanilson is also a viable forward, while defensive-value options include Van Hecke, Milenkovic and Antonio Silva. Spurs have favourable fixtures too, but their defensive assets are more appealing than their attackers, with Pedro Porro a punt and Kinsky an option in goal. Brighton remain worth targeting after Manchester City, while Leeds forwards such as Calvert-Lewin need careful rotation because their fixture list is mixed.

The data raises concerns over Chelsea, who rank bottom for xG per 90 across the past six matches, weakening the case for Palmer and Morgan Rogers at their prices. Manchester City, Bournemouth and Brighton remain among the best attacks, while Bournemouth and Spurs have conceded less expected goals than Arsenal over the last six. Gabriel is nevertheless becoming increasingly attractive: Arsenal's trip to Liverpool is difficult, but managers no longer spending heavily on Palmer, Fernandes or Saka can use that money for Arsenal's highest-upside defender. Gabriel is preferred over less secure Arsenal alternatives, with questions around William Saliba's availability, Ben White and Jurrien Timber sharing right-back minutes, and Riccardo Calafiori's flag and recent benching.

Nicolas Jackson is the preferred João Pedro replacement, although his lack of penalties and occasional early substitutions mean he is not an automatic choice. Dominic Calvert-Lewin offers a safer long-term route thanks to regular 90-minute appearances, penalties and strong data, while Evanilson is a focal point for Bournemouth and Barry is a cheap high-chance option with poor finishing risk. Erling Haaland remains the clear premium forward. Alexander Isak becomes a credible alternative if managers are avoiding expensive midfielders, though his price must be weighed against cheaper forwards plus Liverpool midfield options from Gameweek 10, when Liverpool's fixtures improve after Arsenal.
key_points: Sell João Pedro in most squads after his thigh injury rules him out for Gameweek 9 and likely Gameweek 10, but a transfer-poor team can hold if his post-international-break return is close.
Nicolas Jackson is the leading João Pedro replacement, with Calvert-Lewin, Evanilson and Barry offering different combinations of security, fixtures and price.
Tavernier is the leading midfield buy at £6.4m because Bournemouth combine strong fixtures, strong data and an advanced role for him.
Gabriel is increasingly worth funding despite Arsenal's Gameweek 9 trip to Liverpool, particularly for managers moving money away from underperforming premium midfielders.
Avoid rushing into Chelsea attackers: their xG per 90 over the past six matches is the league's worst, making Palmer less compelling value.
Bournemouth defenders Van Hecke, Milenkovic and Antonio Silva are the preferred long-term defensive additions, while Spurs defensive assets also benefit from a strong fixture run.
Liverpool attackers, including Wirtz, Barcola and possibly Cody Gakpo, become stronger considerations from Gameweek 10 when Crystal Palace begin a favourable run.

items.title: Early transfer made ✅ FPL Gameweek 9 Preview 🔥
items.headline: Haaland remains the clear Gameweek 9 captain as João Pedro injury drives Jackson transfers
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 9 at home to Brighton. Brighton have started well and are not an easy opponent, but there is no alternative with a sufficiently strong combination of form, fixture and reliability to justify backing against Haaland. Cole Palmer at home to Manchester United is the nearest premium option for non-Haaland owners, while Nicolas Jackson against Fulham and Marcus Tavernier against Leeds are acceptable picks but not compelling captaincy candidates. Manchester City’s Haaland, Josko Gvardiol, Ruben Dias, Gianluigi Donnarumma and Elliot Anderson are rested from the Carabao Cup after a short break and are expected to be available to start in Gameweek 9; Gvardiol is viewed as a particularly strong pick because of his attacking upside.

João Pedro is expected to miss at least the next few weeks with a thigh injury and may not return until after the international break. There is no need for managers who have already missed his price fall to rush a transfer before further news, but selling him is reasonable when squad depth is weak. The move made is João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson, driven by Jackson’s long run of favourable Villa fixtures: Fulham at home, Manchester United away, Sunderland at home, Ipswich away, Everton at home, Crystal Palace at home and Coventry away. Jackson’s minutes carry some Champions League-related risk, especially through early substitutions, but his fixtures make him a strong medium-term buy. The trade-off is that holding João Pedro and instead improving a weak bench option, such as moving Sangaré to Tavernier, could prove better if João Pedro returns by Gameweek 11.

A Gameweek 9 Free Hit is viable for managers carrying multiple Arsenal defenders, yellow flags and poor bench cover, but it is not essential. Arsenal visit Liverpool, making clean sheets less likely, while a one-week Free Hit can also sidestep doubts over players such as Riccardo Calafiori. However, the chip lacks obvious explosive differentials because many of the weaker sides play each other. A proposed Free Hit core keeps Haaland and Gvardiol, uses Spurs assets against Crystal Palace including Kudus, and includes Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Tavernier, Thiago and Jackson. Thiago is attractive as a nailed penalty taker who is underperforming his expected goals, while his four yellow cards matter less on a one-week chip. The preferred approach is to save the Free Hit unless it creates a major upgrade over the existing squad.

For a Gameweek 9 Wildcard, Haaland and Jackson are near-automatic inclusions, while the third forward slot depends on structure. Dominic Calvert-Lewin offers minutes and penalties but needs bench cover for tougher away games; Evanilson is a more consistently playable alternative, and Alexander Isak remains defensible. Palmer is retained largely for squad structure and Chelsea’s prolonged good fixture run rather than current underlying numbers. Chelsea’s poor results without João Pedro come from only two matches, so Palmer and Rogers are holds for most managers ahead of Manchester United at home and Sunderland away. In defence, Arsenal’s David Raya and Gabriel are the safest long-term picks, with Calafiori only preferable if fully fit and secure for minutes. Liverpool’s Jarell Quansah is a useful £5.1m route into a defence with four clean sheets in eight matches, but similarly priced defensive-contribution specialists such as Vuskovic, Silva and Murmurovic are preferred by some due to stronger bonus potential and fixtures.

Martin Ødegaard is a hold rather than a buy. He has no goal or assist since Gameweek 3, but his expected goal and assist figures remain respectable, he is playing close to 90 minutes, and Arsenal host Hull in Gameweek 10. Managers with only one or two free transfers are advised not to spend one simply replacing him with a short-term cheaper midfielder such as Manzambi or Tavernier. Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, becomes a significant concern after being benched and not used by Michael Carrick; unless Carrick clarifies the situation, selling Fernandes is sensible due to uncertainty over his next start.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Brighton in Gameweek 9; Palmer is the best fallback for managers without him, but is well behind the Manchester City forward.
Gvardiol is expected to start against Brighton after being rested from the Carabao Cup and offers major attacking upside despite Manchester City rotation risk.
João Pedro is likely out until after the international break, with a Gameweek 11 return possible but far from certain.
João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson is a sound transfer because Villa’s fixtures turn excellent, although Jackson’s European schedule may lead to occasional early substitutions.
Avoid rushing to sell Palmer or Rogers despite João Pedro’s injury, as Chelsea’s bad record without him comes from only two matches and their fixture run remains favourable.
A Gameweek 9 Free Hit is most useful for teams overloaded with Arsenal defenders, flags and weak bench cover, but lacks standout differential options and can be saved.
On a Wildcard, Raya and Gabriel are the safest Arsenal defensive picks; Calafiori is only worth the risk if his fitness and minutes are confirmed.
Hold Ødegaard through Gameweek 10’s home fixture against Hull unless managers have abundant free transfers or a clear long-term upgrade.

items.title: JOAO PEDRO OUT?! ⚠️ | FPL General's GW9 Team Selection
items.headline: João Pedro injury update could force early Nicolas Jackson move ahead of Gameweek 10 Raya plan
items.summary:
The key decision is whether João Pedro’s fitness situation forces an immediate transfer. After using a Wildcard in Gameweek 5 with Joško Gvardiol and Neco Williams in defence, defensive changes have been expected eventually, but injuries and doubts elsewhere have repeatedly taken priority.

Bukayo Saka, Dominik Szoboszlai and now João Pedro create a congested list of potential problems, making reliable injury news on the Brighton forward crucial. The preferred route is João Pedro to Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson, a straightforward swap that addresses the forward concern without disrupting the wider squad plan.

However, the move has a timing problem. The manager has exactly £0.0m spare for João Pedro to Jackson and wants to save enough money to upgrade Kęnski to Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya in Gameweek 10. Jackson may therefore need to be bought within the next day or two to avoid a price change, despite the reluctance to make an early transfer while Saka, Szoboszlai and João Pedro remain uncertain.

The trade-off is clear: waiting for definitive João Pedro news protects against using a transfer unnecessarily, but risks losing the exact budget needed for both Jackson now and Raya next week. The immediate plan depends on whether João Pedro receives a favourable return timeline.
key_points: João Pedro’s injury timeframe is the decisive factor in the transfer plan.
The preferred move is João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson, with no money currently left over.
A Jackson price rise could force an early transfer within the next day or two.
The proposed Jackson move preserves a planned Kęnski-to-David Raya upgrade in Gameweek 10.
Saka and Szoboszlai concerns make an early transfer risky because other squad issues may require attention.
Defensive transfers have been delayed since the Gameweek 5 Wildcard, despite owning Joško Gvardiol and Neco Williams.

items.title: BEST GW9 FREE HIT DRAFT 🔥 | THE FPL SCOUTCAST GAMEWEEK 9 🚨| FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: João Pedro injury makes Nicolas Jackson the priority transfer for Gameweek 9
items.summary:
João Pedro’s confirmed absence for at least the next two gameweeks forces a major FPL decision in Gameweek 9, with Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson emerging as the leading replacement. Jackson has four goals from 2.74 expected goal involvement and now appears secure for minutes, while Villa’s next six include Fulham, Manchester United, Sunderland, Ipswich and Everton. The recommendation is to move early if possible, with Pedro expected to fall in price and Jackson set to rise, rather than leaving money tied up in an injured forward. Alexander Isak remains an appealing premium alternative because of his bonus-point potential, but Arsenal at home is a poor entry fixture and his higher price compromises future moves for Gabriel or other premium defenders.

Erling Haaland remains the clear captaincy choice despite Manchester City facing Brighton. Brighton are strong, but there is little confidence in the alternative premium options: Cole Palmer is out of form despite a favourable Manchester United fixture, Pedro is unavailable, Bukayo Saka is injured and Bruno Fernandes is unreliable amid United’s instability. Palmer is still viewed as a strong Gameweek 9 pick rather than a captaincy contender, with Chelsea expected to exploit a vulnerable United side.

Bournemouth assets are rising up the agenda after their 3-0 win at Manchester United and an attractive fixture run beginning with Leeds at home. Marcus Tavernier is the preferred attacking option at £6.4m due to set pieces, strong underlying numbers and more reliable minutes than Evanilson, who could lose minutes or penalties when Kroupi returns. Antoine Semenyo is also a viable long-term purchase, particularly for defensive-contribution points: Bournemouth are not considered elite defensively, but Semenyo’s regular DefCon potential gives him a useful floor through Leeds, Ipswich and Fulham. Evanilson is less convincing as a new buy because Kroupi’s return creates added selection risk.

A Free Hit is viable in Gameweek 9 for managers whose squads are heavily invested in Arsenal and lack Chelsea, Villa, Bournemouth or Newcastle coverage. A draft built around Haaland, Palmer, Jackson, Tavernier, Morgan Rogers, Antoine Semenyo and DefCon defenders such as Van Hecke and Lewis Hall can attack the week while fading Arsenal’s trip to Liverpool. However, it is not an automatic chip week: many of the desirable players are strong long-term purchases anyway, and Arsenal’s defence is still capable of a low-scoring result at Anfield. Managers with multiple free transfers are encouraged to buy the needed assets rather than use the chip, while those with a weak XI and no route to Jackson, Bournemouth players or Chelsea attackers can consider the Free Hit.

The broader advice is to avoid unnecessary transfers beyond Pedro’s replacement. Morgan Gibbs-White continues to post encouraging chance-creation and shooting numbers despite recent blanks, so he is a hold for managers short of free transfers. Arsenal’s defensive assets should not be sold solely because of Liverpool away, although Gabriel remains a future priority over less secure options. Holding transfers after the Pedro-to-Jackson move preserves flexibility and funds for the next defensive reshuffle.
key_points: Move João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson promptly if possible, with Pedro ruled out for at least two gameweeks and price changes expected in both directions.
Captain Erling Haaland against Brighton; the premium midfield alternatives lack form, fitness or reliability.
Marcus Tavernier is Bournemouth’s preferred attacker because of set pieces and stronger minute security than Evanilson.
Antoine Semenyo is a strong Bournemouth defensive pickup for clean-sheet upside and frequent defensive-contribution points.
Evanilson carries increased rotation and penalty risk when Kroupi returns, making him less appealing as a fresh transfer.

A Gameweek 9 Free Hit can target Chelsea, Aston Villa, Bournemouth and Newcastle while opposing Arsenal at Liverpool, but managers with spare transfers should generally buy players they want long term.
Hold Morgan Gibbs-White if transfers are limited: his recent underlying numbers remain encouraging despite three blanks.
Avoid spending heavily on Isak before Arsenal at home unless squad structure can absorb the cost; Jackson offers the better immediate fixture run.
